# COR062 `stat-without-errmsg`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

An `allocate`/`deallocate` has `stat=` but no `errmsg=`.

## Why

`stat=` only tells that the statement failed; `errmsg=` gets the runtime's explanation (already
allocated, out of memory, ...). Without it the error handler can only print a number.

## Reported

```fortran
allocate(a(n), stat=ierr)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
allocate(a(n), stat=ierr, errmsg=msg)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR062] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR062` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C183` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
